summary: Iteration 2 backend testing for Online Vaidhyaji AYUSH. Added /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py with 13 new tests covering doctor registration_number field, appointment default fields (paid=false, amount==doctor.consultation_fee, prescription=null), mock payment flow (POST /pay success + 404), prescription flow (patient can add, third-party 403, unknown appt 404), GET /api/prescriptions filter (only appts with prescription!=null), and health-records vault CRUD (add, list, user-scoping, delete, 404, auth-required). Full regression suite green: 38/38 tests passed (25 previous + 13 new). No backend code changes required.

minor.issue: documents_uploaded is set to bool(registration_number) — a bare non-empty string like ' ' would count as uploaded. Not user-facing yet, but consider stripping/validating registration_number.
Endpoint is idempotent: paying an already-paid appointment succeeds again and refreshes paid_at. Not a bug for MVP mock payment, but for real Stripe this would need an idempotency guard.

Comment says 'Either the patient (demo) or the doctor of the appt can add'. In practice the appointment's doctor_id is a seeded doctor UUID (not a user account UUID), so a real registered doctor user's id will typically NOT match doctor_id — meaning today only the patient can add. If a real doctor-side workflow is planned, link appointment.doctor_id to a users collection id.

action_items: Consider adding a follow-up endpoint or field for doctor verification (admin flow) since verified defaults to False on registration.

If a real doctor-side prescription workflow is required, link appointment.doctor_id to the users collection (currently it references the seeded db.doctors collection UUID which does not overlap with registered doctor-user accounts).
Optional: strip/validate registration_number so documents_uploaded reflects a real value; currently bool(' ') is True.
critical_code_review_comments: New endpoints (pay, prescription, reports) correctly scoped by user_id/patient_id — third-party access returns 403 (prescription) or is silently filtered (reports).
MongoDB _id continues to be excluded via projection {'_id': 0} on all new reads; pop('_id', None) used on new writes.
ReportInput allows optional image_base64 — no size cap; consider limiting payload size to protect Mongo document 16MB ceiling (e.g., FastAPI request size limit or explicit Field(max_length=...)).
list_prescriptions correctly builds compound query {patient_id/doctor_id, prescription: {$ne: null}}.
Payment endpoint mutates appt in-place and returns fresh copy — response is the full updated document (good).
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py (new — 13 tests, 6 test classes, one third_party_patient fixture)
seed_data_creation: No changes to server seed. Tests create disposable TEST_ users (test_<uuid>@vaidhyaji.example.com), TEST_-prefixed reports, and short-lived appointments. Not cleaned up but isolated by uuid and TEST_ prefix.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite lives at /app/backend/tests/. Full run: `python -m pytest backend/tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. Use conftest.py fixtures: patient_ctx, doctor_ctx (session-scoped). For 403 tests use the module-scoped third_party_patient fixture in test_new_features.py. Public URL is read from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env. Pydantic EmailStr rejects .test/.example TLDs at the second-level — use vaidhyaji.example.com. Note: appointment.doctor_id currently references seeded db.doctors UUIDs (not user IDs), so 'doctor can add prescription' branch of POST /appointments/{id}/prescription is only reachable if the doctor's user.id == appointment.doctor_id, which is not possible with the current schema. This branch is covered by code review; direct end-to-end testing would require schema change.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no failures encountered. All 13 new tests passed on first run; full 38-test regression is green.
